what_was_missing: Nothing was absent. Every section 4 function and constant exists (now 88 exports: the 87 found plus removeFile). Every bracketed section 3 format has its schema file (58 files). All 58 load and pass the closed-keyword check. Every name a script or test imports from lib exists. The shipped tcb/thresholds.json (all section 3.20 names present), profiles/*.json and every fixtures/*/*/case.json validate against their schemas.

Corrected PATTERNS.task to the contract's section 1.5 pattern (device name followed by end or '.'). The draft also refused a device name followed by '-' to fit spec/lib.md T2's 'con-research'. The contract wins, and the lib test writer asserted acceptance from the contract.
Corrected realProc().alive: removed the process.kill(pid, 0) ESRCH shortcut. It answered false while PowerShell was unavailable; section 4.9 and T89 require null whenever PowerShell fails.

Corrected slotCount (section 4.10, T96). A 'never admitted' filter ran before the process match. An attempt that had only a folder therefore counted 0 even with a live matching process, and was skipped when procList was null. The order is now the contract's: unconfirmed; procList null -> unknown; matched process -> live; current admitted/started/bound attempt or last attempt of a committed row -> unknown; transcript -> unknown. Each epoch is counted once. Without a root, a relative folder's transcript is found through a project folder whose first cwd ends with that folder.

Corrected intakeCandidates' in_flight (spec/check-queue.mjs.md step 2 and T14). A batch whose queue/<b>/ folder exists without batch.json is ignored. A batch.json of another mode is ignored. A sealed key with no queue folder still counts.

Completed validate's cross-file $ref resolution. With no run root known, it now reads the schemas folder beside lib.mjs. `resolve` may be a function or a string naming a run root or a schemas folder. A missing file or definition is still an error entry, never a throw.
parseTranscript memory: the run-text buffer kept the text blocks of every message id in an assistant run; it now keeps only the last id's (matters for T79b).

parseTranscript shapes: turn-end `open` is now non-enumerable, so turnEnds entries are exactly {ts, text}. Added a non-enumerable `line` to tool uses, tool results and structured entries (U2a's request for harvest's source.line).
currentDesign now returns exactly {cut_sha, hazards_id, hazards_sha}. The stpa/fmea choice by the same rule (U1a's request) is now non-enumerable stpa_id, stpa_sha, fmea_id and fmea_sha.
checkerVerdicts now returns exactly {verdicts, reasons, duplicates, unknown_items}. The extra details and unknown_ids are now non-enumerable.
child_process is now used through its default export at call time, so a test spy on the module (T88) reaches the library.

paths(root): added the keys builders asked for: commitRecord, statusDir, cutFile, heldoutOf, plantKey, plantDir, blindKey, frozenFile, protocolDraft, plantCandidatesOf, auditFile, auditSearch, auditCoordinator, snapshotRaw/Text/Meta, byUrlFile. Existing keys are unchanged.
Added export removeFile(path) with the section 4.3 sharing retries (U1a's request).
Schema repair: causes[].card_id may be null. tms writes null for pack-repaired and questions-changed, which the draft schema refused.
Schema by-url: 'reason required when raw_sha is null' (section 3.13) is now enforced with an anyOf.
deviations_from_the_spec: spec/lib.md T2 lists `--task con-research` as exit 66; the library follows CONTRACT 1.5 and accepts it (the contract is the source of truth).
projectDirName replaces every non-alphanumeric character (kept from the draft). It is identical on the contract's listed characters and on T82's example.
parseTranscript takes a parseable last line that lacks a trailing newline as a record and moves endByte past it (kept from the draft). A torn line never parses, so T78 holds.
intakeCandidates' in_flight adds check-queue's batch.json and same-mode rule to CONTRACT 4.10's wording.
slotCount takes an optional 4th argument {root} that is not in the contract's signature; all callers pass three.
currentProtocol accepts the sha of the file's bytes or of its canonical form, and a root-relative or absolute path.

Extras beyond the contract's shapes are non-enumerable. The enumerable extras kept from the draft are parseTranscript's `reset`, readLedger's `badLines`, fence's `changed` and `rev`, and calls' `partial`.

A lock file whose record does not parse is never judged stale (section 4.4 defines staleness only through proc.alive). Every acquirer then waits and exits 75 until a person removes the file. This is unchanged from the draft and is fail-safe.

tcb/test/lib.test.mjs and four other test files import ../scripts/lib.mjs. In the flat layout lib is tcb/lib.mjs: change the imports to ../lib.mjs, or add a shim tcb/scripts/lib.mjs containing `export * from '../lib.mjs';`.

That a real session's command line carries the session id (`--resume=<id>`). process-facts.md says the cwd is not on the command line, so folder matching will rarely hit (T92).
The permissionDecision field on tool-result records of helper transcripts.
Whether a helper's StructuredOutput input and its structured_output attachment always agree. Both are listed, so checkerVerdicts counts an equal repeat in `duplicates`.

slotCount with procList null counts every attempt not known ended, including a never-run attempt that a 'first' fence created (for example on a row cut before any start). While PowerShell fails, such entries count as unknown forever. This is fail-safe, but narrowing it needs a contract change.
intakeCandidates: a check-queue run cut off after the sealed key and before queue/<b>/ exists keeps those cards in flight until --requeue.
T79b depends on the fixture's shape. The contract requires keeping every call, tool input, result and turn-end text, so a fixture whose bulk is in tool inputs can still exceed a 64 MB heap.
